You had one job: generate a 384 bit private keys and instead you used: 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, and 237.

This allows attackers to issue certificates for any websites.

Embarrassing that it’s a family business run by largely computer illiterate people. Only 1 of the 3 have a remotely computer-related background and even they never actually worked a technical job in their life. Imagine how many attacks you can design with AI given the existence of this genre of gross negligence.

candidates.text:
something very interesting is happening in the outbound space and Ive not been able to make sense of it - 

Just one year ago - accessing quality b2b user data was a hard problem. 

you had to scrape apollo, verify leads, pay expensive fees per 1000 people , you then had to verify every lead, remove bad emails, bad catch all's + remove the ones with inbox protection etc 

building lists, setting up infra etc were hard problems to solve. 

now moltsets, quick enrich, coldiq have all come up with offers where you get unlimited access to all b2b data via api for a fixed cost. 

you can also but a @smartlead_ai  plan for $300/mo and send half a million emails a month

or you can spin up an infra with microsoft inboxes that sends 500k emails a day (A DAY!) for $6000/mo 

The cost of data has now become negligible. The cost of setting up infra has now become negligible. The cost of personalizing messages (although poorly) is also really low. 

I have no idea what happens to sales and outbound from here , because this seems more like a bubble with everything becoming commoditized and cheap and easily accessible to everyone.

Time will tell

candidates.text:
The last 20 years were about bits. The next 20 are about atoms.

For two decades, the best software engineers went to work on getting you to watch one more video, buy one more thing, or click one more ad. Smart people, hard problems. But when you shipped, a number on a dashboard went up 0.3%, and nobody outside your team noticed.

Now the world is turning back to atoms: rockets, factories, robots, energy. Every one of them runs on software, and the best software jobs in the world are not at software companies. They are at places like @relativityspace, @zipline,  @CFS_energy and @valaratomics.

Nothing compares to seeing your PR take physical form. At @relativityspace, you ship code and factory machines build rocket parts, an engine lights on the test stand, telemetry streams down from the edge of space, and a ship in the middle of the ocean tracks a falling rocket and steers itself to the exact spot where it will land. Your commit did that.

Come write code you can see and hear from a mile away.
